Simulate observation data for an edge model

Source: R/simulations.R
simulate_bison_model.Rd

Simulates observations of social events in an undirected network with known edge weights. Use it to try out bisonR functions, to learn the format of the data, or to check that a model recovers the true values before using it on real data.

Usage

simulate_bison_model(
  model_type,
  aggregated,
  location_effect = TRUE,
  age_diff_effect = TRUE,
  num_nodes = 10,
  max_obs = 5
)

Arguments

model_type

Type of data to simulate, "binary" (whether an event occurred in each sampling period) or "count" (the number of events).

aggregated

If TRUE, observations are summed to one row per dyad, with the location column removed. If FALSE, there is one row per observation.

location_effect

Whether location affects the probability or rate of events.

age_diff_effect

Whether the age difference between the two nodes affects the probability or rate of events (by 0.2 per unit of age difference on the link scale).

num_nodes

Number of nodes in the simulated network.

max_obs

Maximum number of observations per dyad. Each dyad gets between 1 and max_obs.

Value

A list with df_sim, the simulated observations, and df_true, the true edge weights on the link scale. df_sim has columns node_1_id, node_2_id, event and effort (observation effort), and predictors. It also has a duration column, identical to effort, for code written for earlier versions; new code should use effort. The true edge weights in df_true don't include the effects of age difference or location.

Details

Each dyad's true edge weight is drawn from a standard normal distribution on the link scale (log-odds for binary data, log rates for count data). Each node gets an age, and each observation takes place at one of five locations, each with its own effect. Binary data have one sampling period (effort 1) per observation; count data have an observation effort drawn uniformly between 1 and max_obs.

See also

simulate_bison_model_mixture(), bison_model()

Examples

sim_data <- simulate_bison_model("binary", aggregated = FALSE)
head(sim_data$df_sim)  # Observations
#>   node_1_id node_2_id event effort age_diff    age_1    age_2 location duration
#> 1         1         2     1      1 2.946436 23.37606 20.42962        4        1
#> 2         1         2     1      1 2.946436 23.37606 20.42962        4        1
#> 3         1         2     1      1 2.946436 23.37606 20.42962        3        1
#> 4         1         2     1      1 2.946436 23.37606 20.42962        1        1
#> 5         1         2     0      1 2.946436 23.37606 20.42962        3        1
#> 6         1         3     0      1 2.688601 23.37606 20.68746        5        1
head(sim_data$df_true) # True edge weights (on the logit scale)
#>   node_1_id node_2_id edge_weight age_diff    age_1    age_2
#> 1         1         2   1.3930343 2.946436 23.37606 20.42962
#> 2         1         3  -0.5495812 2.688601 23.37606 20.68746
#> 3         1         4   1.1436925 2.818835 23.37606 20.55722
#> 4         1         5  -0.7115225 9.347903 23.37606 14.02815
#> 5         1         6  -0.6320064 2.483173 23.37606 20.89288
#> 6         1         7  -0.0657349 7.461969 23.37606 15.91409
